title: Work with a timer, then take a break
group: LDS-FOCUS — Focus and Getting Things Done
examples: How long should I work before a break?
How can a timer help me focus?

explain.say: Imagine your focus is like a phone battery. It runs down, and then it needs charging. A break is your charger. Look at the board. It shows a work time, then a break, step by step.

faq.q: How long should my timer be?
faq.a: Start short, like 5 or 10 minutes. When that feels easy, you can make it a little longer. A grown-up you trust can help you choose.
asks: Tell me about Set the timer

faq.q: What can I do in my break?
faq.a: Move your body, stretch, jump, get a drink or look out of the window. Keep screens for later, because they make it hard to stop.

faq.q: How do I go back after a break?
faq.a: Set the timer again before you start your break. When the break timer rings, sit down and pick up your pencil.
asks: Tell me about Back to work
How do I stop my break?

faq.q: What if I stop before the timer rings?
faq.a: That is okay. Notice it, take a breath and start again. Next time, try a shorter time.
A timer shows you the work will end soon. That makes it easier to start and to keep going.

facts: Working in short blocks with breaks is a well-known study method, sometimes called the Pomodoro method.
The Pomodoro method was named after a tomato-shaped kitchen timer.

quiz.say: The timer rings. What do you do?
quiz.why: The ring means work time is over. Now you have a short break.

wrong.1: Your focus needs a charge. A break helps.
wrong.2: The timer is your helper. Keep it where you can hear it.

quiz.say: What is a good first timer length?
quiz.why: Ten minutes is short enough to feel easy. You can make it longer later.

wrong.1: Two hours is very long. Start short and grow.
wrong.2: One second is too short to get anything done.
